stories.s: The Courts and Tribunals Judiciary reports that Dame Victoria Sharp has retired from the judiciary as President of the King's Bench Division. The notice, dated 1 October 2026, points to a longer piece on her tenure and the changes she led in the Division. The item is a judicial appointments update for England and Wales.

stories.t: Protocol for publishing judgments in Welsh and English
stories.s: The Courts and Tribunals Judiciary describes a pilot scheme testing whether judgments can be published in both Welsh and English. The pilot applies to the Administrative Court in Wales. The notice is dated 1 October 2026. The item concerns court publication practice in Wales.

stories.t: Modernisation of High Court structure comes into effect today
stories.s: The Courts and Tribunals Judiciary says the Business and Property Division of the High Court took effect on 1 October 2026. It brings together courts previously spread across the Chancery and King's Bench Divisions. The change restructures how commercial and property cases are allocated within the High Court in England and Wales.

stories.t: Child defendants in the Crown Court – sixth edition
stories.s: The Courts and Tribunals Judiciary has published the sixth edition of its bench book on child defendants in the Crown Court. The guide gathers in one place the material a Crown Court judge or recorder needs on the subject. The notice is dated 30 September 2026 and concerns criminal court practice in England and Wales.

stories.s: Doug Austin's eDiscovery Today summarises important 2026 court rulings on artificial intelligence and says Exterro sets out the main trends from them. The post is commentary that points readers to Exterro's analysis rather than reporting the rulings directly.

stories.s: Doug Austin reports that Meta's Muse AI agent reportedly builds profiles of people in users' lives, including people who do not use Muse. The claim is reported rather than independently confirmed.

stories.t: Current Methods to Identify AI Content: Artificial Intelligence Trends

stories.s: Victoria Cash of Casepoint discusses where PDF-centric FOIA workflows begin to break down, in a guest post on eDiscovery Today. The commentary covers eDiscovery best practice for public records requests.

The story notes concern that the syllabus covers too much law. The report is dated 12 October 2026. The proposals affect future solicitor qualification candidates in England and Wales.

stories.s: Legal Cheek reports that a former A&O executive has co-founded an AI law firm. The venture is described as taking aim at the billable hour. The extract is brief and gives no names, dates or funding details.

stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports alarm at plans to remove a defendant's right to elect jury trial while increasing magistrates' sentencing powers. Volunteers are described as unequipped to try complex, multi-day trials.

stories.t: Conditions could be imposed on barristers awaiting misconduct hearing
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports that the Bar regulator will be able to impose conditions on barristers awaiting misconduct hearings, a halfway point between normal practice and interim suspension.

stories.s: The Welsh government's counsel general says talks were held with Burnham on justice devolution and that a separate Welsh jurisdiction is back on the table. The Law Society Gazette reported the remarks on 12 October.

stories.t: Uncertainty surrounds PM's pledge on 'non-compete' clauses
stories.s: The Prime Minister has pledged to legislate against non-compete clauses as a drag on innovation, according to The Law Society Gazette. The government's announcement gave few details, leaving its approach uncertain.

Solicitor lied to court with backdated letter in attempted cover-up
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports on a solicitor who tried to argue he had served a claim form on the right party, after producing a backdated letter that the court found to be a cover-up attempt.

stories.t: 'Positive' steps made as small firms talk face-to-face with SRA
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports that small firms have talked face-to-face with the Solicitors Regulation Authority and that the talks produced positive steps. Reforms due to take effect in January are now on hold while discussions with the regulator continue. The report is dated 12 October 2026.

stories.t: IBA 2026: Embattled US judges will be 'history’s heroes', says former American bar chief
stories.s: At the IBA 2026 conference, a former American bar chief said embattled US judges would be remembered as history's heroes. The Law Society Gazette reports that law firms which did not bend to Trump are thriving.

stories.t: Court of Appeal hands down guidance on judges sentencing remotely
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports that the Court of Appeal has issued guidance on when judges may pass custodial sentences remotely. According to the report, such circumstances will be rare. The report is dated 9 October 2026 and concerns sentencing practice in England and Wales.

stories.s: Mishcon de Reya has published key takeaways from its 2026 Insolvency Litigation: Future Leaders Seminar. The notes cover administration, practitioner powers and the use of effective evidence in court. The extract gives no further detail on the discussion.

stories.s: Mishcon de Reya says Mandy Xu has joined its Hong Kong office as Of Counsel, strengthening the Disputes department. The announcement is dated 12 October 2026. The extract does not give her prior firm or practice area detail beyond disputes.

stories.t: Conflicting Birkenstock copyright rulings: Cassandra Hill comments in World IP Review
stories.s: Cassandra Hill of Mishcon de Reya comments in World IP Review on conflicting rulings over Birkenstock designs. A Dutch court ruled for Birkenstock against Lidl, while a 2025 German ruling rejected copyright protection for the same footwear. The comment highlights the difficulty of protecting functional designs through copyright in Europe.

stories.t: The Government renews its pledge to restrict non-compete clauses
stories.s: Mishcon de Reya reports that Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the Innovation Nation Summit in Manchester that the Government will legislate to restrict non-compete clauses in employment contracts. The article was published on 9 October 2026. The firm's account is the basis for the report, and the detail of the planned legislation is not yet set out.

stories.s: Mishcon de Reya has published Issue 5 of its Inside Disputes newsletter, dated October 2026. The issue covers litigation, AI, sanctions and commercial cases, and looks at how English court practice is changing. It is a firm-produced publication.

stories.t: Growth & talent in the UAE: Opportunity, risk and the legal toolkit
stories.s: Mishcon de Reya's article on growth and talent in the UAE says the country has moved from a regional commercial hub to a destination for senior professionals in financial services, technology and professional services. It cites a favourable tax environment and a developing legal and regulatory framework. The extract is partial.

stories.t: California’s COMPETE Act: Single-Firm Conduct Will Face Antitrust Scrutiny Under California Law in 2027
stories.s: Paul Hastings reports that Governor Gavin Newsom signed A.B. 1776, the COMPETE Act, into law in California. The firm says single-firm conduct will face antitrust scrutiny under state law from 1 January 2027. The alert, dated 9 October 2026, sets out a new regulatory risk for businesses operating in California.

stories.t: Department of Justice’s Fraud Division Issues Corporate Enforcement Directive
stories.s: Paul Hastings reports that the US Department of Justice's Fraud Division issued a memorandum on 1 October 2026 setting out corporate enforcement principles and priorities. Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald issued it. The firm says the division will apply these principles in its enforcement work.

stories.t: National Law Journal: DOJ Doubles Down on Data Analytics; Compliance Programs Must Keep Pace
stories.s: Paul Hastings partners Roberto Gonzalez and Sam Kleiner, writing in The National Law Journal, discuss US Department of Justice signalling that it will invest more in data analytics and technology. They urge compliance officers to devote sufficient resources to keep pace.

stories.t: DOJ Revises Justice Manual to Limit Reliance on Agency Guidance and Expand Qui Tam Dismissal Review
stories.s: Paul Hastings reports that the US Department of Justice revised two sections of the Justice Manual on 18 September 2026. The changes govern False Claims Act enforcement, including limits on guidance documents and review of qui tam dismissals. The alert is dated 7 October 2026.

stories.t: Daily Financial Regulation Update -- Tuesday, October 6, 2026
stories.s: Paul Hastings' daily financial regulation update for 6 October 2026 covers federal financial regulators. It reports that FinCEN withdrew proposed rules on digital assets that would have imposed recordkeeping, verification and reporting duties, with the withdrawal dated 5 October 2026. The extract is partial, so other items in the update are not visible.
